## Part 1
### Setup

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)
breeding <- read.csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")
gt(breeding)
```
```{r}
colnames(breeding)
glimpse(breeding)
```
```{r}
print(nrow(breeding))
print(ncol(breeding))
print(dim(breeding))
##dim refers to dimensions: showing both rows and columns
```
### Migration site CSV file
```{r}
mig <- read.csv("data/migratory_connectivity_dataset.csv")
gt(head(mig, 10))
```

### Pipe symbol
Pipe symbol |> is an Operator that is used to link multiple steps in an analysis: passes values on Left to empty function on the right
```{r}
my_numbers <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)

print(sqrt(sum(my_numbers)))

print(my_numbers |>
  sum() |>
  sqrt())

my_result <- my_numbers |>
  sum() |>
  sqrt()
print(my_result)
```


Excersize

```{r}
input_vec <- c(5, -10, 4, -3)

output_vec <- input_vec |>
  mean() |>
  abs() |>
  round()

print(output_vec)
```

To only show relevant columns, Pipe data to function select()
```{r}
select(breeding, Site, Longitude, Latitude)

bird_breeding_selected <- breeding |>
  select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename (Breeding_Longitude = Longitude, Breeding_Latitude = Latitude)

gt(bird_breeding_selected)
```

Core excersize
```{r}
bird_migration_selected <- mig |>
  select (
    Site, 
    winterLongitude, 
    winterLatitude, 
    pslon, 
    pslat, 
    iblon, 
    iblat, 
    awestlon,
    awestlat
    ) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename(Winter_Longitude = winterLongitude, Winter_Latitude = winterLatitude, Stopover_Longitude = pslon, Stopover_Latitude = pslat, Iberian_Longitude = iblon, Iberian_Latitude = iblat, Westmost_Longitude = awestlon, Westmost_Latitude = awestlat)

gt(head(x = bird_migration_selected))

```
Comparison Operators: ==, !=, >, >=, <. <=. Returns true/false. 

Function: filter(), uses comparison operators

```{r}
bird_breeding_exc <- bird_breeding_selected |>
  filter(Site != "Spain")
gt(bird_breeding_exc)

bird_migration_exc <- bird_migration_selected  |>
  filter(Site != "Spain")
gt(bird_migration_exc)
```

## Part 2
Find median values for each migration location for bird_migration_exc
trhough function group_by() and summarise()
(Glimpse gives brief overview, shows groups. Groups do not modify data, only modifies data operations)
```{r}
bird_migration_grouped <- bird_migration_exc |>
  group_by(Site)
gt(bird_migration_grouped)
glimpse(bird_migration_grouped)
```
Summarise() used from this point on to calculate specific statistics per Group
You can do multiple summary statistics in 1 summarise function

na.rm = TRUE argument tells R to ignore any rows with a value of NA. 
```{r}
lat_df <- bird_migration_grouped |>
  summarise(
    Highest_Lat_Stopover = max(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Lowest_Lat_Stopover = min(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Lat_Stopover = mean(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Highest_Lat_Winter = max(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Lowest_Lat_Winter = min(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Lat_Winter = mean(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

gt(lat_df)
```

Excersize time

```{r}
bird_migration_summary <- bird_migration_grouped |>
  summarise(
    Stopover_Longitude = median(Stopover_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Stopover_Latitude = median(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Iberian_Longitude = median(Iberian_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Iberian_Latitude = median(Iberian_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Westmost_Longitude = median(Westmost_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Westmost_Latitude = median(Westmost_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Winter_Longitude = median(Winter_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Winter_Latitude = median(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE), 

  )

gt(bird_migration_summary)
```
### Joining Data Frames
uses a Join:
full_join() has All the rows from both data frames with NA when no data valiable
inner_join() has ONLY the rows that have data from both data frames
left_join has all data in first data frame and adds data from 2nd when avaliable (NA if not)
right_join has all data in 2nd data frame and adds data from 1st when avaliable (NA if not)
Site column is shared between breeding and migration tables. All sites present in all frames, so any type of join here is the same. 
```{r}
combined_bird_data <- full_join(bird_breeding_exc, bird_migration_summary)
gt(combined_bird_data)
```
### Long and Wide Formats

Using a Long format: contain everything in location type so each bird has multiple rows
Use pivot_longer()

*Arguments* for pivot_longer:
> Select columns to reshape using cols
> Split column names using names_sep
> Create new column names using names_to

```{r}
combined_bird_piv <- combined_bird_data |>
  pivot_longer(
      cols = ends_with(c("_Longitude", "_Latitude")),
      names_sep = "_",
      names_to = c("Location_Type", ".value")
  )
gt(combined_bird_piv)
```

### Subsetting data frame
Make 2 subsets: 1 for spring, 1 for autumn. 
Spring has breeding stopover winter, Autumn has breeding iberian westmost winter. 

filter() function is used here again, but pass Vector of values using operator %in%: 

therefore can filter rows on Multiple values at once! (from One column)

(unlike before, which was one at a time)


make a new vector here, holding the lists of groups you Want

```{r}
Springful <- c("Breeding", "Stopover", "Winter")

spring_data <- combined_bird_piv |>
  filter(Location_Type %in% Springful)
gt(spring_data)

Autumnful <- c("Breeding", "Iberian", "Westmost", "Winter")

autumn_data <- combined_bird_piv |>
  filter(Location_Type %in% Autumnful)
gt(autumn_data)

```
Save these as new csvs
```{r}
write_csv(spring_data, "output/birds_spring.csv")
write_csv(autumn_data, "output/birds_autumn.csv")
```

## Part 3
geom_point() adds scatterplot points
Specific to plotting maps:
annotation_borders() adds geographical country borders
Add country borders and add a map.


```{r}
ggplot(spring_data, aes(
  x = Longitude,
  y = Latitude)) + geom_point() + annotation_borders(linewidth=0.2) + coord_quickmap()
```

set axis limits (refer to this again for sbR)
use min() and max() functions 
pull() takes single column from a data frame


```{r}
min_lon <- spring_data |>
  pull(Longitude) |>
  min()
max_lon <- spring_data |>
  pull(Longitude) |>
  max()
min_lat <- spring_data |>
  pull(Latitude) |>
  min()
max_lat <- spring_data |>
  pull(Latitude) |>
  max()
```
add as axis limits using coord_quickmap and xlim and ylim as vector, subtract 2 from each min and add 2 to each max

```{r}
ggplot(spring_data, aes(
  x = Longitude,
  y = Latitude)) + geom_point(size=3) + annotation_borders(linewidth=0.2) + coord_quickmap(xlim = c(min_lon-2, max_lon+2), ylim = c(min_lat-2, max_lat+2))
```

Make points big: add argument size to geom_point()

Group points by setting color and etc in aes()
Add labels of measruement and minimal theme trhough ggtitle() and theme_minimal()
Add paths connecting each point for same breeding pop through geom_path() and aes(group = Site) since will make lines by site
```{r}
ggplot(spring_data, aes(
  x = Longitude,
  y = Latitude, color = Site, shape = Location_Type)) + geom_point() + annotation_borders(linewidth=0.2) + coord_quickmap(xlim = c(min_lon-2, max_lon+2), ylim = c(min_lat-2, max_lat+2)) +
  ggtitle("Pied Flycatcher Spring Migration Routes") +
  xlab("Longitude (°)") +
  ylab("Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_path(aes(group = Site))
```
